title: MURCIÉLAGO
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Serial killer Kuroko Koumori, on death row for killing 715 people, has her execution stayed in exchange for hunting criminals the police cannot catch. With driving expert Hinako and yakuza boss's daughter Chiyo, she takes on cases against killers, cults and gangs, killing with gleeful brutality while chasing her own sexual appetites.
life_message: It presents a killer licensed to kill killers, played as over-the-top dark comedy where bad people meet bad ends.

content.note: Extreme violence tending to guro, said to get worse later (Okazu review); AniList Gore 97%, Body Horror; MU Blood and Gore, Serial Killer/s.
Psychopathic killers and grotesque deaths (Okazu review; MU Insanity, Psychopath/s).

Frequent lesbian sex scenes and nudity (Okazu 'Service 10'; MU Cunnilingus, Tribadism, BDSM, Borderline H; AniList Nudity 92%); MangaDex erotica. MU also lists 'Rape' and AniList Rape 35% (to verify).
Crude, perverted dialogue (Okazu review describes the series as crude); MU Black Humor.
Psychopathy and dissociative identities played for horror (AniList Dissociative Identities 35%) (to verify).
A protagonist who enjoys killing and sexual predation is the comic hero (Okazu review: 'evil, psychotic and perverted'; MU Villain Protagonist).

folkways.japan: The police quietly outsourcing killings outside the courts and the deadpan seinen black comedy reflect Japanese seinen action conventions rather than everyday Japanese norms.

delivery.evidence: Okazu review (per entry) calls the heroine evil, psychotic and perverted, played as dark comedy; delivery itself not discussed (to verify).

delivery.note: The story presents lethal vigilante justice as comedy without a voice for legal restraint.

winners_losers: Kuroko wins and is the sympathetic center; criminals are killed as deserving it. Legal process and restraint lose.
